stories.title: Overnight attack on St Petersburg oil terminal and depot kills one, injures five
stories.summary: An overnight strike hit the St Petersburg Oil Terminal and the Ruchyi oil depot, killing at least one person and injuring at least five. Governor Alexander Beglov said fires were being extinguished at both sites. Kyiv has not commented, while President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia has hit Ukraine’s energy sector 76 times since the “energy ceasefire” was announced.
stories.why: The attack targets Russian oil facilities that provide revenue for Moscow’s war effort.

stories.title: Trump suspends Russia sanctions as US‑Ukraine tensions rise
stories.summary: Donald Trump issued an executive order on Friday night suspending a number of Russia sanctions that were scheduled to take effect two days later; the sanctions had been passed by Congress and signed into law in September. The move drew criticism from US lawmakers and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, while Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev praised it as historic. Relations between Washington and Kyiv have recently deteriorated after a US deal to import Russian diesel and Ukrainian accusations of reduced military support.
stories.why: The suspension changes US policy toward Russia, strains the US‑Ukraine alliance, and could affect US and global financial markets.
stories.previousTitle: Trump suspends upcoming Russia sanctions, heightening dispute with Ukraine
stories.previousSummary: President Donald Trump issued an executive order on Friday night to block several sanctions on Russia that were scheduled to take effect in two days. The sanctions, passed by Congress and signed into law in September, were halted on the grounds of U.S. national interest, prompting criticism from U.S. lawmakers and a sharp rebuke from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev called the move historic, while tensions have risen after a U.S. deal to import Russian diesel and Ukraine’s claim that the administration reduced military aid.
stories.change: No material change since the previous brief.

stories.title: India notifies first tariff cuts under New Zealand FTA
stories.summary: India will apply customs‑duty concessions for certain New Zealand imports starting October 20, the first tranche of the bilateral free‑trade agreement. The schedule gives zero basic duty on sheep meat, sets specific reduced rates for fish and wine, and assigns particular duties to manuka honey and kiwi fruit, while dairy products are excluded.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.
stories.previousTitle: India to Apply First Tariff Reductions Under New Zealand Free Trade Agreement
stories.previousSummary: Starting 20 October, India will grant customs‑duty concessions on selected New Zealand imports under the bilateral FTA. The concessions include a zero basic customs duty on sheep meat, specific rates on fish and wine, and varied duties for manuka honey and kiwi fruit. Dairy products are excluded from the liberalisation.
stories.change: No material change since the previous brief.

stories.title: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to visit India next week
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel to India next week for his second visit this year. He will hold meetings in Mumbai and Jamnagar that will focus on investment and energy issues. The trip comes as both sides grapple with lingering delays in finalizing a U.S.-India trade agreement.
stories.why: The visit aims to reinforce bilateral ties and advance the stalled trade negotiations.
